card: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in CConnman to prevent duplicate connections to the same target. Concurrent manual connection attempts—such as overlapping -connect and -addnode arguments during startup—race past existing duplicate checks because those checks only inspect peers already added to m_nodes. Target addresses and hostnames are now reserved during OpenNetworkConnection() so concurrent attempts are rejected while a dial is pending. This addresses long-standing issue #5299 and includes a functional test verifying rejection of overlapping attempts held in a proxy handshake.
changed_since_previous: The core approach remains unchanged from the previous description.
evidence: Fixes #5299 ('Initial connection management'), an open issue from 2014 documenting duplicate outbound connections on startup.
Follows closed PR #27804 ('init: deduplicate added connections') and addresses overlapping connection issues noted in #22559.
problem: Concurrent manual connection attempts to the same target—such as overlapping `-connect` and `-addnode` startup arguments or concurrent `addnode onetry` RPCs—race past existing duplicate checks. Because existing checks only verify connected peers already present in `m_nodes`, multiple outbound connections to the same remote peer can be established before either attempt finishes.

risk.why: A bug in connection in-progress tracking or destination normalization could mistakenly reject legitimate manual connections or prevent retrying failed manual peers.

summary: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in `CConnman` using a set of destination keys to prevent duplicate connections. When `OpenNetworkConnection()` attempts a manual connection, it registers the target in `m_manual_connection_in_progress` and clears it upon exit using an RAII guard. Any concurrent attempt to dial the same normalized address or hostname string is rejected while the first attempt is pending.
